An October 2026 follow-up by the same authors adds Supervisor and Meta Reflection mechanisms for open-ended tasks where intermediate metrics are lacking; with web access disabled, agents rediscovered on average 62.7% of the finding criteria drawn from three ICLR oral papers. The follow-up task code is released under Apache-2.0.

name: ScienceFlow
domain: Long-horizon machine-learning and computational scientific research
inputs: Research task packages, model credentials, isolated workspaces and compute budgets
outputs: Recoverable experiment states, validated results, search branches and execution records
notes: Huawei Noah’s Ark Lab framework that couples persistent research workspaces, evidence gates and adaptive continuation or re-anchoring with compute scheduling. The author-owned noah-research monorepo releases the framework, tasks and documentation under MIT. The paper’s physical jobs are compute jobs, not laboratory actuation.

name: Brain Researcher
inputs: Research questions, admissible neuroimaging datasets and approved analysis plans
outputs: Versioned analysis episodes, artifacts, provenance and condition-tagged review verdicts
notes: Connects evidence, analysis choices and tool execution through a workspace with a researcher commitment gate. Public MIT code includes the CLI, MCP contracts, service stack and examples. Private benchmark corpora, knowledge-graph contents and site-specific launchers are excluded; the paper’s broad archive wording must not be read as public access to every study asset. Interpretation remains with researchers.

name: Orchestra (regulatory discovery)
inputs: Gene/network comparison queries and configured RegNetAgents and CASCADE evidence services
outputs: Regulator candidates with independent-source support and source-level evidence flags
notes: MIT LangGraph workflow composing regulatory-topology and experimental-evidence MCP services. Tests whether agreement between evidence sources enriches known cancer-gene annotations; it does not establish causal regulation or prospective wet-lab discovery. This CASCADE dependency is Jose Bird’s bioinformatics service, distinct from the catalogued scientific skill-learning CASCADE.

name: ARCHE
inputs: Mechanistic research questions, chemistry tools and configured reasoning models
outputs: Prioritized mechanisms, executed computational investigations and evidence-revised conclusions
notes: The paper combines general and chemistry-specialized models with a tool registry for iterative mechanistic investigation. Its author-linked Arche-Harness release is a later investigation_v2 implementation, not the paper’s earlier Planner/Execution/Reflection system. ARCHE-Chem weights, reward model, training corpus and training pipeline are absent; the public code and selected case data do not reproduce the complete paper configuration. A custom academic/non-commercial license applies. Closure is computational; reviewed sources were the primary abstract and repository documentation, not inaccessible HTML full text.

access_evidence.software_license: Academic and Non-Commercial Research License v1.0

name: La Agente Óptima
domain: Agentic Bayesian-optimization campaigns on digital and physical laboratories
inputs: Scientific objectives, experiment search spaces, BO-MCP optimizers and connected laboratory platforms
outputs: Executable campaigns, measurements, repaired constraints and feedback-guided experiments
notes: Demonstrated on five digital tasks and two physical platforms. A real contact-angle loop executed measurements and revised a failing campaign, with operator approval for constraint changes and restarts; physical deck preparation requires a named human certification. Public research artifacts include data, conversations and plotting code, not a verified complete deployable Óptima system. The artifacts repository has no confirmed license, so public visibility is not an open-source claim.

name: Modelica Agent Workflow Benchmark
domain: Modelica model repair, generation and parameter tuning
inputs: Faulty models, engineering requirements or tuning targets with OpenModelica validation
outputs: Executable and behavioral task checks under a shared agent evaluation protocol
notes: Companion benchmark to Pufibara. Public v0.2 provides Apache-2.0 code, protocol and schemas plus a small demo split under a separate Benchmark Data License: academic/non-commercial evaluation and local smoke testing are permitted, while model training, distillation, training-data expansion and dataset redistribution require written permission. Official evaluation uses hidden maintainer-run sets. Neither the full task set nor the full Pufibara stack is released; modeling is computational.

access_evidence.software_license: Apache-2.0 code; custom Benchmark Data License restricts task data to specified uses and prohibits training/distillation and dataset redistribution without permission

name: PACE-Bench
domain: Adaptation of code-driven designs to changed simulated physics
inputs: 144 source-to-target environment pairs across six physics domains with a limited attempt budget
outputs: Adapted designs, sandbox feedback, validity checks and adaptation success scores
notes: Tests whether agents can repair a formerly successful design after a change in simulated physics while preserving goal and interface. Public MIT harness includes task environments and executable validation. Distinct from PACE-SIMS, which concerns a physical mass-spectrometry instrument.

name: Andy (mathematical research)
domain: Mathematical problem generation and proof workflows
inputs: Mathematical problems, proposed proofs and optional reference papers
outputs: Proof dependency graphs, separately reviewed proof steps, new problems and traceable reports
notes: MIT research system with a local workspace, persistent proof state and separate generation and checking models. Failed proof nodes trigger targeted repair. Automatic checking is language-model-based and is not equivalent to a formally verified proof-assistant certificate; the README requires researcher review before formal use.

name: Benchmark-as-Teacher (BaT)
domain: Evaluation and recursive post-training harness for medical-imaging research agents
inputs: Stage-level research rubrics, held-out-safe training states and an agent model
outputs: Targeted training curricula, updated agent checkpoints and repeated stage-level evaluations
notes: NVIDIA-associated MIT framework connecting stage diagnostics, data generation, GRPO training and evaluation gates for medical-imaging research agents. The public repository implements the training loop; it does not establish prospective clinical usefulness or a wet-lab loop. Distinct from the AutoMedBench evaluation resource it uses.

name: OmniScientist (omni-modal, NUS/Oxford)
domain: Research from raw multimodal evidence to executable analyses and manuscripts
inputs: A research direction and local raw multimodal scientific data
outputs: Hypotheses, executed code, analyzed figures, traceable results and manuscript artifacts
notes: MIT system by Bobo Li, Hao Fei and collaborators with perception, ideation, experiment and writing stages. The September desktop release replaces the discontinued standalone terminal edition; a coding-agent skill remains available. Independent identity from Tsinghua FIB Lab’s 2025 OmniScientist: different authors, paper and repository. Demonstrations are computational.

name: GeneBench-Pro
domain: Multistage statistical analysis in genomics, quantitative biology and translational biomedicine
inputs: Brief context, a target estimand and staged data files in an offline sandbox with Python/R scientific and genomics libraries
outputs: A JSON answer of numerical estimates, graded pass/fail against reference values recoverable from the agent-visible data under calibrated tolerances
notes: OpenAI benchmark of 129 agentic analysis problems across 10 primary domains with a genomics-centred core; successor to GeneBench. Each problem has 3-13 dependent analysis decision points. Only 10 externally reviewed problems are public, as an MIT-licensed Hugging Face package with prompts, staged data, ground truth and a reference grader; the answers are intentionally public and no agent runner is included. 50 held-out problems went to Artificial Analysis and 69 remain internal. All data are simulated from known data-generating processes, although the public task prompts tell the agent the data came from a real experiment; there is no laboratory component.

name: AFMBench
domain: Atomic force microscopy instrument-operation and data-analysis agent evaluation

paper_links.label: arXiv (preprint title: Autonomous Microscopy Experiments through Large Language Model Agents)

inputs: 100 natural-language AFM tasks, tagged basic or advanced, single or multiple tools and agents, and documentation, analysis or calculation requirements
outputs: Graded task scores (1 correct, 0.5 partial) with operational and token metrics for four LLM backbones, plus a single- versus multi-agent comparison on a 10-task subset
notes: Benchmark from an IIT Delhi-led team, introduced with the AILA (Artificially Intelligent Lab Assistant) multi-agent framework and published in Nature Communications (2025). Instrument-operation tasks run on a physical Nanosurf DriveAFM through its Python API; analysis tasks read stored .nid image files. GPT-4o, GPT-3.5-turbo, Claude 3.5 Sonnet and Llama-3.3-70B were scored: strong materials-science QA performance did not carry over to instrument workflows, and agents sometimes departed from instructions, including unrequested tip movements. Disclosed safeguards: documentation for critical operations was withheld from the agents and those operations left to trained staff; no human review of agent actions was implemented. Running the instrument tasks needs the vendor hardware and API. Tasks, code and per-model response logs are MIT-licensed. The AILA agent itself is not represented by this row.

name: HeurekaBench
domain: Open-ended data-driven research questions on experimental datasets (single-cell instantiation)
inputs: Open-ended or multiple-choice research questions with single-cell datasets; questions are built from published studies and their code repositories and checked against reported findings
outputs: Data-driven answers scored against validated published findings (multiple-choice accuracy; open-ended answers rated by a GPT-4o judge)
notes: EPFL (Brbić lab) framework for building co-scientist benchmarks from published studies and their code; ICLR 2026. Its single-cell instantiation, sc-HeurekaBench, has 50 open-ended and 50 multiple-choice questions over 41 validated insights, plus lite and tool-use splits; the paper evaluates Biomni, CellVoyager and BixBench-Agent. Code and question files are MIT (licence added September 2026); the ~44 GB datasets are on Hugging Face. Agents perform computational analyses only.

name: DrugTargetWorld
domain: Causal drug-target discovery in simulated biobanks
inputs: Procedurally generated biobank worlds of 54,000 synthetic participants (genotypes, proteomics, health records, outcomes, synthetic cine-MRI) with a budgeted service for simulated experiments
outputs: Disease phenotype, ranked causal driver proteins with modulation direction, optional rejected decoys and abstentions, scored 0-100 against the hidden causal ground truth
notes: Stanford-led environment for training and benchmarking AI agents on end-to-end drug-target discovery in cardiovascular biobank worlds whose causal structure is known to the scorer but hidden from the agent. Version 1 evaluated nine agents in 540 episodes across 20 worlds and three experimental budgets. The purchasable 'wet-lab' experiments are simulated interventions, so closure is computational. The MIT-licensed GitHub repository holds documentation only; the generator, oracle, scorer and harness source is marked 'Coming Soon', and the benchmark runs from a prebuilt Harbor image. World data on Hugging Face are gated: generated tables are MIT, ACDC-derived cine-MRI falls under ACDC terms, and a full sweep needs about 345 GB.

name: ScienceClaw (Skill-Operator self-evolution)
domain: Program-level self-evolution of AI-for-science agents across 23 ANZSRC research divisions (natural sciences, social sciences and humanities)
inputs: Scientific tasks with inputs, tools, evaluators and hard constraints, presented as sequential task streams
outputs: Replay-verified workflow results, versioned Skill and Operator updates, and ScienceClaw-Eval scores
notes: Agent system built on the OpenClaw gateway by authors from CUHK-Shenzhen, NTU, Duke-NUS and others. A workflow repair becomes a linked Skill and typed Operator only if a clean replay reproduces it, hard constraints hold and independent validation tasks improve within budget. The batch evolver applies this gate automatically; in gateway use, candidates wait until the user promotes them, and promotions can be rolled back. MIT code (the LICENSE file keeps the upstream OpenClaw copyright line). The ScienceClaw-Eval data on Hugging Face contain only the held-out IID and OOD splits (64 records each per discipline) under row-level upstream licences, some non-commercial or share-alike. Unrelated public projects share the name ScienceClaw (e.g. lamm-mit, AgentTeam-TaichuAI, Zaoqu-Liu); this record covers beita6969/ScienceClaw only.

name: MMPostTrainBench
domain: Autonomous post-training research on a multimodal base model
inputs: Qwen3-Omni-30B-A3B-Instruct base model, development-evaluator feedback and a fixed budget (eight GPUs, default 24 h per loop) on one of eight image, audio, video, audio-video and multimodal-coding tasks
outputs: Submitted models scored by a separate verifier on held-out tests for target gains and non-target regressions, with candidate-selection analysis and operator-side research-integrity audits
notes: Multimodal fork of PostTrainBench (per the repository NOTICE) from USTC with Alibaba Group co-authors. Agent and verifier run in separate containers; the agent has no shell access to held-out evaluation data or verifier code, and integrity auditing runs on the operator side. MIT code, task packages and container recipes; upstream models and datasets are downloaded separately and some require access approval. Requires a Linux GPU host with Docker. The MMResearch controller proposed in the paper was not found in the repository on 2026-10-10.

name: Open-Endedness Bench (OEB)
domain: Process evaluation of open-ended agent research from execution records
inputs: Execution records of agents on open-ended research tasks, converted to OEB's record format (converters provided for three benchmarks)
outputs: Epistemic event graphs; scores on four competence axes (evidence, experiment, revision, no reward hacking); six descriptive persona traits
notes: ARA Lab with authors from Michigan, MIT, Ohio State and UC Davis. Scores how an agent forms, tests and revises claims from its execution record alone, without reference answers or outcome scores. LLM judges extract acts and claims with exact quotes, which code checks against the record, and answer closed questions by majority vote; code does all counting. Has no task set of its own: the paper scores 119 existing runs from PostTrainBench, Chip-Bench and the nanoGPT speedrun (ML and hardware engineering tasks). Judge outputs and call logs are released. MIT code; the paper's scored runs are on Hugging Face under CC BY 4.0. Measures research process quality, not the correctness of final results.

name: OSWorld-Science
domain: Computer-use agents operating professional scientific software

repo_links.label: Hugging Face (gated data and VM images)

inputs: 146 expert-defined tasks across seven domains and 17 scientific software tools, run in KVM virtual machines through screenshot-based GUI and optional command-line actions
outputs: Partial-credit scores from task-specific evaluators that inspect generated artifacts and application state, plus trajectories and cost reports
notes: Multi-institution benchmark (Tsinghua, Yale and others) covering chemistry, physics, medicine, statistics, biology, GIS and linguistics workflows in tools such as QuPath, ASKCOS, OpenFOAM and PyMOL. The paper treats ScienceBoard as related work; the two are separate benchmarks. The repository is CC BY 4.0, while task data, grader references and VM images are CC BY-NC 4.0 behind manual Hugging Face approval; third-party software keeps its own terms. Public images contain no licensed software: SAS and Mnova steps need the user's own licences, and the 14 Ansys Fluent tasks need a self-built Windows guest and an Ansys licence. Requires Linux x86-64 with KVM and Docker. The published data include answer keys.

access_evidence.software_license: CC-BY-4.0 repository (not a software licence); task data, graders and VM images CC-BY-NC-4.0 behind manual approval; third-party and licensed software under own terms

name: BIABench
domain: End-to-end bioimage analysis reconstructed from published studies
inputs: 16 tasks with raw 2D, 3D and time-lapse images and basic or expert instructions
outputs: Outcome scores against study ground truth plus VLM-judged process scores
notes: Benchmark of 16 tasks from H&E histology to single-molecule localization microscopy, with adapters for Claude Code, Codex, DeepSeek Harness, Biomni and two Fiji-based agents (CopilotJ, Agentic-J; the authors co-developed Agentic-J). The harness is BSD-3-Clause. Task data on Hugging Face (11.1 GB zipped) keep per-task source licences (CC BY 4.0 or 3.0, CC BY-SA 4.0, CC0, GPL-3.0, and EMBL-EBI Terms of Use for one task), and the authors' own specs, rubrics and derived ground truth are CC BY 4.0. Part of the work used ELIXIR Estonia infrastructure at the University of Tartu.

name: MolDesignBench
domain: Scenario-grounded molecular generation and optimization with chemistry tools
inputs: 2,000 design narratives (1,800 feasible, 200 infeasible) with implied and explicit property and functional-group constraints
outputs: Proposed molecules or infeasibility judgements, scored with and without 17 chemistry tools (success, constraint satisfaction, infeasibility accuracy, validity, tool calls)
notes: Korea University and LG AI Research benchmark (COLM 2026) for tool-augmented LLM agents, capped at 20 interaction turns per instance. The best evaluated agent reaches about 43% success. Two property-range design tools require an NVIDIA MolMIM NIM with NGC credentials. Code is MIT; the benchmark questions on Hugging Face are CC BY-NC 4.0 and, per the dataset card, also subject to the Terms of Use of the model used to create them (Claude Opus 4.6). Computational scoring only; no synthesis or wet-lab validation.

access_evidence.software_license: MIT code; CC-BY-NC-4.0 benchmark questions, which the dataset card also makes subject to the Terms of Use of the generating model (Anthropic Opus 4.6)

name: MechBench
domain: Mechanism discovery beyond phenomenological laws from observational data
inputs: Observational training data and scientific context for each task; hidden mechanistic models, including mutated variants of canonical mechanisms, generate the data
outputs: Observable-law accuracy on train, in-distribution and out-of-distribution data, plus mechanism-probe scores
notes: Benchmark from a Tsinghua University-led team (repository in the tsinghua-fib-lab GitHub organization). It scores two things separately: recovery of an observable law and recovery of the hidden mechanism behind it. The Full-set has 512 synthetic instances from 16 task families in physics, chemistry, biology and materials science, built as mutated variants of canonical mechanisms. The paper evaluates Codex, Claude Code and DeepSeek Harness configurations. Scoring uses symbolic equivalence and numerical accuracy with no LLM judge. The repository is MIT-licensed, forked from yuzhTHU/mdbench. It bundles the task library, task-validation, export and scoring code, and baseline run results. Not the same system as MECHBench (arXiv 2511.10821), a black-box optimization benchmark from structural mechanics.

name: RECLAIM
domain: Reproducing central empirical claims of machine-learning papers
inputs: 100 NeurIPS 2025 papers (plus a 14-paper development split), each with whatever its authors released, a fixed target value with tolerance, and a GPU budget of up to 96 H100-hours; Run, Retrain and Reimplement tiers
outputs: Per-run 0-10 audit score and verdict (reproduced, partial, not reproduced, unverifiable, disqualified) assigned by an LLM auditor from logs and outputs; per-tier reproduction rates
notes: Salunkhe, Ding, Verma, Kindratenko (UIUC/NCSA). Tiers follow what the authors released: code, data and weights (Run), no weights (Retrain), no code (Reimplement). Claude Sonnet 5 grades each run from execution evidence, not the agent's own report (F1 0.82 against human graders). Of four agents tested, the best per tier reproduced 41% (Run), 27% (Retrain) and 15% (Reimplement). Designed to be rebuilt yearly from new conferences. MIT code; splits and 372 run records under CC BY 4.0, also on Hugging Face; the repository still describes itself as an anonymized release under review.

name: TraceML
domain: Development-process comparison of ML-engineering auto-research agents with human Kaggle practice
inputs: A finished ML-engineering agent run (git sidecar with scored tags, AIDE/MLEvolve search journal, or git workspace tracking submission.csv); for recording new runs, any command-line agent plus MLE-bench-prepared competition data
outputs: Version-level trajectory with state and action labels in the dataset schema, and a behaviour report comparing the run with 4,465 human Kaggle trajectories and the paper's Codex and MLEvolve runs
notes: Carnegie Mellon dataset and toolkit that records ML development as scored, labelled code versions. On seven Kaggle competitions it pairs 430 human trajectories with 207 agent trajectories from 31 Codex CLI and MLEvolve runs (MLEvolve searches split into branches), showing agents stuck in narrow edit loops. Apache-2.0 toolkit and labeler models; dataset mostly CC BY 4.0 (GPT-5-mini labels may not train competing LLMs). Labelling needs a CUDA GPU. ML engineering only. Not the Polyaxon or TraceOpt 'traceml' tools.

name: SA-Bench (SemanticAlign-Bench)
domain: Semantic fidelity of agent-generated ML paper-reproduction code
inputs: Paper specification plus an agent-generated reproduction repository for each of 30 ICLR, ICML and NeurIPS 2025 ML papers
outputs: Five-level per-claim scores over 1,491 human-verified Semantic Alignment Units, aggregated into numerical, method, protocol and ordering drift diagnostics
notes: Benchmark by authors at Beihang University, Shanghai Jiao Tong University, Minzu University of China and Peking University (corresponding author at Peking University). Accepted to Findings of EMNLP 2026 according to the arXiv comment. It measures semantic drift, where reproduction code runs but departs from the paper's specification. Scoring is static: dimension-specific LLM judges compare code text against atomic implementation claims, and the generated code is never executed. A deterministic mode without an LLM judge is also available. ML papers only. Ships BasicAgent, PaperCoder and OpenHands baseline runs. MIT code; CC BY 4.0 annotations on Hugging Face.

name: DeltaML-Bench
domain: Improving published baselines inside real machine-learning research repositories
inputs: 48 tasks sourced from Papers With Code, each with the paper PDF, original code repository, dataset and published baseline metric, run under time and token budgets
outputs: Percentage improvement over the published baseline, per-run success rates and integrity checks for specification gaming
notes: Algorithmic Research Group benchmark run on METR's Vivaria platform. The paper compares GPT-5 and Claude Sonnet 4 under a modular scaffold and ARG's search-based scaffold, and reports specification-gaming rates up to 47.9% in modular runs. The public repo ships task families, anti-cheat checks, graders and modular agents; the ARG agent folder named in its README was removed in March 2026. Root licence Apache-2.0; the bundled Vivaria and task folders carry METR MIT licences. Most tasks need a GPU, Docker and model API keys.

name: ExplorationBench
domain: Hypothesis-driven exploration of executable rule worlds that conflict with prior knowledge
inputs: A flawed manual, fixed worked examples and a single probing tool with deterministic feedback, over four exploration rounds per sandbox (AlienCode, AlienLogic)
outputs: Rule reports and held-out task answers from tool-disabled copies at each milestone, checked exactly by an interpreter or proof checker (no LLM judge)
notes: Benchmark from Fudan University, Tencent Hunyuan and Tsinghua University that measures whether AI systems acquire unfamiliar rules by probing an alien calculation language (AlienCode) and a patched natural-deduction logic (AlienLogic): 55 discovery targets, 140 held-out tasks, ten frontier systems evaluated. Apache-2.0 code releases the harness, scoring, evaluation engines and two small demo worlds; the evaluation worlds stay private, so leaderboard scores require a maintainer-run evaluation and demo scores are not comparable. The worlds contain no science-domain content, and the authors state the benchmark does not measure real scientific discovery.

name: AgentIdeaBench
domain: Scientific ideation under static versus agentic literature access
inputs: Subfield name plus a Semantic Scholar search/fetch tool with a 10-call budget (Active) or the subfield plus 5 fixed reference papers (Static); 100 subfields in five disciplines, 40 densely scored
outputs: One-paragraph hypotheses scored 1-10 by three LLM critics against retrieved prior art on originality, feasibility, clarity, impact and specificity; Static-vs-Active leaderboard and released scores and search traces
notes: HKUST KnowComp benchmark (with NVIDIA co-authors) reporting matched static and active evaluations of 33 LLMs. Active retrieval separates models more than static reference sets do. Scores are LLM-critic judgments; the authors note that originality is the least validated dimension. Code is MIT and released data are CC BY 4.0. Measures idea generation; hypotheses are not tested experimentally. Distinct from IdeaBench (asa-ideabench).

name: SciExam for ENSO
aliases: AI Science Exam for El Nino-Southern Oscillation
domain: Building low-order stochastic ENSO climate models from observations
inputs: Raw ocean-atmosphere observations for 1980-2014, background material and a reference paper; a six-hour budget split into data processing, diagnostic writing and model building
outputs: Agent-built stochastic ENSO models scored by hidden graders on ENSO statistics, recovery of unobserved variables and forecasts of held-out years (2015-2024); released runs and checkpoints
notes: Benchmark by authors from Ohio State, Yale, UC San Diego, Stanford and Princeton. Agents process observations into indices, write their own diagnostics, which are then frozen, and use only those as feedback while building the model. Hidden numerical graders, with no LLM reviewer, score each model and a published reference model the same way; twelve agent systems are evaluated. The sciexam code and the agent-written model files are MIT; the other released records are CC BY 4.0, with third-party data terms listed. Sandboxed grading uses Docker, and rerunning agents needs the user's own provider accounts. Computational modelling only.

name: WhatWorkedBench
domain: Inferring experimental effects of workflow changes under measurement budgets
inputs: Executable workflow code, two free anchor measurements (all-zero and all-one configurations) and a budget of purchasable measurements, across 36 task conditions
outputs: Predicted response surfaces scored on component effects, interactions, configuration choice and delivery
notes: Carnegie Mellon and Tsinghua benchmark of how much research agents learn from a limited number of experiments; references come from exhaustive native CPU execution. Apache-2.0 release with the task catalog, budgeted evaluator, numerical baselines and replay evidence; third-party datasets keep their upstream terms, some limited to scientific use. Workflows are ML tasks such as classification, forecasting and image restoration; the paper evaluates DeepSeek V4 Flash and Pro agents.

name: Ascent
domain: Pharmacoepidemiological analysis of real-world clinical data
inputs: Natural-language epidemiological questions and cohort eligibility criteria over OMOP-CDM or native-schema clinical warehouses, through a shared Model Context Protocol tool server
outputs: Medical code lists, SQL, patient cohorts with attrition funnels and baseline summaries, and answers with inspectable intermediate results
notes: Bayer AG system used internally for expert-supervised analysis of real-world clinical data. An LLM orchestrator plans, calls medical-coding, question-answering, cohort and SQL tools on a shared Model Context Protocol server that any MCP client can drive, inspects intermediate results and re-plans; underspecified questions go back to the user to confirm an interpretation. The public BSD-3-Clause distribution is a demonstration on generated patients and synthetic vocabularies, ships the EpiTrap set of designed-in pharmacoepidemiological errors, and needs an external LLM API key. Reported gains over a fixed pipeline came with more tool calls and longer runtimes; evaluation used one Optum EHR source with LLM grading, and the system does not estimate causal effects.

name: LabAgent
domain: Reproducing and extending a laboratory's computational life-science methods
inputs: A laboratory's code repositories or papers, a reproduction target or analysis task, staged datasets and a run budget
outputs: Execution-validated skill packages, reproduced metrics and figures with scripts and logs, benchmark answers, and a memory of failure fixes
notes: Yale-led harness, with Northeastern, Broad Institute and Stanford co-authors. Its explore stage turns a repository or paper into a skill that enters the library only after it installs and runs end to end; its reproduce stage executes the skill on mini-swe-agent and reads back commands that fixed failures in earlier runs. Evaluated on drug-property prediction (TDC ADMET), biomedical data analysis (BiomniBench-DA, GeneBench-Pro), protein variant-effect prediction (ProteinGym) and statistical-genetics fine-mapping, where it partly rebuilt a figure from the authors' own laboratory: two of the five methods were agent-written surrogates and one ran with a misread flag. Comparisons with Claude Code and Codex use one run per target. MIT code ships the 63 skills used in the manuscript; the repository states that BiomniBench tasks were scored by keyword overlap instead of that benchmark's LLM judge. Setup uses an Anthropic API key. Computational only, no laboratory execution.

name: T-REX (agentic binder design)
domain: De novo protein binder design campaign control
inputs: A design target, available GPUs, a campaign duration and an output directory
outputs: Structurally distinct in-silico binder hits with campaign archives for analysis
notes: Princeton (Zhong lab) framework in which planner and supervisor LLMs, run as a locally served Qwen model via vLLM, decide whether to rescue, explore or exploit while a deterministic controller validates and schedules generation, redesign and evaluation jobs across Proteina-Complexa, BindCraft and BoltzGen. Across seven targets it allocated compute in a target-dependent way and yielded more structurally distinct in-silico hits than the baselines evaluated (PUCT, epsilon-greedy, generator-only and SMAC3); the paper states it was assessed only computationally and that experimental validation of its designs remains to be done. The T-REX code is MIT, with a verified installation profile targeting Linux and H100 GPUs under Slurm; the orchestrated backends and model assets keep their upstream licences, PyRosetta included.

name: MOMbot
domain: Robotic multimodal interventions on Xenopus embryos, organoids and cells; closed loop demonstrated on organoids
inputs: Operator-loaded biological material, a human-specified objective and a stimulus search space (in the closed-loop demonstration, electrical-stimulation duration from 1 to 300 s)
outputs: Interventions chosen by the active learner and executed on the robot, image-derived organoid velocity measurements and an updated duration-response model
notes: Robot scientist from the University of Vermont, Tufts University and Harvard (Wyss Institute, Harvard Medical School) with five two-dish stations, four stimulus modalities (chemical, electrical, mechanical, thermal) and high-resolution imaging; the hardware was validated on Xenopus embryos, mucociliary organoids and dissociated ectodermal cells. In the closed-loop demonstration an upper-confidence-bound active learner chose electrical-stimulation durations and the robot applied them to 55 motile mucociliary organoids over eight rounds (about 12 hours across two days), updating the model after each round from a warm start of 29 random interventions. A human operator loads biological material and assigns each dish to AI or human control. No language model is involved. The MIT-licensed repository holds the AI/control software and figure-reproduction data; the custom hardware is described only in the paper.

name: MicroClaw
domain: Natural-language microscope control and adaptive image acquisition
inputs: Natural-language acquisition requests, a Micro-Manager-controlled microscope, a user-reviewed safety configuration and the user's own Anthropic API key
outputs: Executed imaging workflows, compiled Pycro-Manager scripts and inspectable session histories
notes: Microscopy agent from Max Perutz Labs, University of Vienna, and collaborators. It drives Micro-Manager microscopes through Pycro-Manager using Claude models via the Anthropic API. The authors call it pseudo-agentic, and most use is collaborative workflow development. On real instruments it also scanned coverslips with agent-written analysis hooks, switched channels and acquired time-lapses without user input. Disclosed gates: a user-defined safety configuration is enforced before every hardware call; enabling illumination and above-threshold acquisitions require user confirmation, which can be granted per session; agent-written hooks need explicit user approval before they run. The repository says the safety features are not comprehensive and the BSD-3-Clause release is a preview not suited to production. Acquired data and session history files are on Zenodo under CC BY 4.0. It is unrelated to the identically named OpenClaw-family chat assistants on GitHub, such as microclaw/microclaw.

name: LabscriptAI
domain: Liquid-handling robot scripting and gated execution for synthetic biology
inputs: Natural-language experimental intent or community protocols, human-confirmed standard operating procedures, and robot hardware and deck constraints
outputs: Simulator-validated platform-specific robot scripts (Opentrons Python, PyLabRobot, Tecan .gwl), gated runtime recovery actions on Opentrons robots, execution traces, and repository-formatted records (protocols.io, FPbase)
notes: Execution-aware agent harness from the Shenzhen Institute of Synthetic Biology (Chinese Academy of Sciences) with Shanghai Artificial Intelligence Laboratory co-authors. An authoring loop turns a human-confirmed SOP into a platform-specific liquid-handling script and repairs it against simulator feedback (Opentrons Flex and OT-2, Hamilton via PyLabRobot, Tecan Fluent .gwl worklists). A runtime loop reads Opentrons controller state after a failed command and proposes a bounded recovery, which a deterministic gatekeeper allows, holds for more evidence or human confirmation, or suspends; live recovery was tested on an Opentrons Flex only (six matched fault pairs). Reported deployments include cell-free characterisation of 854 GFP designs from 171 student teams in the CAPE 2025-2026 challenges, containment-aware engineering of a formaldehyde-converting enzyme, and robot scripts for assembling 531 genetic parts into the 2025 iGEM Distribution Kit, with manual purification and inter-station transfers where needed. Experimental goals stay human-defined; the authors state that adaptation based on biological outcomes was not tested, and the README leaves sequence screening in deployment to the operator. The README and package metadata declare MIT, but the repository has no LICENSE file and the v3 preprint says code will be provided in a subsequent version, so access is source-available; the Zenodo deposit holds CC BY 4.0 study data without source code.

name: iCloudBiofoundry
domain: Cloud-accessible agentic design with robotic execution for synthetic biology
inputs: Natural-language research objectives entered in the platform's web interface, optionally with prior experimental data or uploaded literature
outputs: Designs, hypotheses and wet-lab protocols; simulation-checked robotic workflows that run at connected biofoundries after administrator approval; measured results returned to the user for the next design round
notes: Cloud platform from the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign (Huimin Zhao laboratory). The iBioGenie multi-agent layer plans work from literature, databases and computational tools; BiofoundryAI compiles its protocols into simulation-checked workflows for the iBioFAB and iBioFoundry robotic facilities. Case studies: phytase re-engineering seeded with data from an earlier campaign, PAND enzyme discovery followed by a second engineering round on the best hit, and CRISPR knockout engineering of yeast beta-carotene production. Human gates: researchers approve plans, administrators approve every instrument job, an operator sets up and starts each run, and the authors chose the second-round PAND target and manually finalised the 32 discovery candidates. Portal access needs federated sign-in and an administrator-approved request. Source code is promised on acceptance; the four GitHub repositories the portal lists returned 404 on 2026-10-10, and the Momentum scheduler is a commercial Thermo Fisher product.

name: Andromeda 2 (Intrepid Labs)
domain: Agentic pharmaceutical formulation design in an automated laboratory
inputs: Target product profile, permitted excipient composition grid with hard constraints, structured in-house formulation evidence, automated formulation laboratory
outputs: 16-formulation SEDDS batches with rationales, prepared by liquid-handling robots and assayed automatically (biorelevant dissolution with HPLC, dynamic light scattering), followed by successor batches informed by the measurements
notes: Language-model agentic system from Intrepid Labs (Toronto), the successor to the company's non-agentic probabilistic optimiser Andromeda 1. Proposal, critique, review and planning steps call the Andromeda 1 models and other tools; a deterministic feasibility engine checks each batch before robotic preparation and automated assays. In one six-batch (96-formulation) paclitaxel campaign per arm, 50% of its formulations reached the pooled upper-quartile AUC threshold, against 17% for Andromeda 1 and 2% for a wet-lab DoE; 12, 6 and 0 met all four target-product criteria. Endpoints are in-vitro dissolution, and the authors note single campaigns limit inference. A formulation scientist reviewed every batch before execution without changing it, and all arms shared the same operators. The paper describes no code, model or data release.

name: cryoAgent
inputs: Cryo-EM movies (or pre-corrected micrographs) with microscope and acquisition parameters, approximate particle diameter, expected symmetry and CryoSPARC project settings
outputs: Three-dimensional reconstructions with quality metrics, heterogeneity (structural-state) analyses, processing-state histories, LLM logs and end-of-run reports
notes: Agent from Fei Sun's group (Guangzhou Institutes of Biomedicine and Health and Institute of Biophysics, Chinese Academy of Sciences) that runs a reason-act-observe loop over CryoSPARC jobs with three autonomy levels: a rigid baseline workflow, guided optimisation and heterogeneity analysis, then hypothesis-driven exploration of alternative processing strategies. It also searches the CryoSPARC forum to recover from job failures. The authors report better reconstructions than the automated workflow cryoWizard on the datasets compared, and a previously unreported isolated 60S ribosome population in EMPIAR-10028 found by the heterogeneity agent. Processing is computational only, on existing EMPIAR data; the microscope is not controlled. Apache-2.0 code; a licensed CryoSPARC installation (tested up to 4.7.1) and an external LLM API are required, and the RELION interface is experimental. Distinct from unlicensed GitHub projects named CryoAgent by other developers.

name: PRAXIS (protein engineering)
domain: Autonomous protein engineering in a robotic laboratory
inputs: Parent enzyme sequences, a defined combinatorial sequence space and substrate-specificity objectives
outputs: Designed variants built and characterised by the robotic laboratory, with an updated sequence-function model
notes: Platform from Philip Romero's laboratory at Duke University, with a co-author at Harvard Medical School, that couples a ProteinNPT-based generative protein language model to an automated laboratory doing gene assembly, cell-free expression and fluorescence enzyme assays. Three agents sharing one learning model ran 25 rounds over about one month without human intervention and shifted Family 1 glycoside hydrolase specificity toward non-native sugars; 132 variants were characterised, and top variants were later re-assayed by hand for verification. Humans stocked the laboratory with all DNA fragments and reagents before the campaign began. It builds on the same group's earlier SAMPLE self-driving laboratory. Apache-2.0 code covers the agent, the in-silico deep-mutational-scanning benchmarks and the laboratory-environment software; the agent and benchmarks run with no laboratory hardware, while wet execution needs the physical platform. The preprint text itself is CC BY-NC.

name: Autonomous enzyme engineering platform (iBioFAB)
aliases: A generalized platform for artificial intelligence-powered autonomous enzyme engineering
domain: Autonomous enzyme engineering on a biofoundry
inputs: A protein sequence and a quantifiable fitness assay, with a natural-language (LLM) interface for campaign setup
outputs: Robot-built and assayed variant libraries, fitness measurements and an improved enzyme variant per round
notes: Platform from the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign (Zhao laboratory) combining an ESM-2 protein language model, the EVmutation epistasis model and a low-N supervised model with the iBioFAB biofoundry, which automates mutagenesis PCR, DNA assembly, transformation, colony picking, plasmid purification, expression and enzyme assays. Four rounds over four weeks screened 446 AtHMT and 448 YmPhytase variants, giving a 16-fold improvement in halide methyltransferase ethyltransferase activity (and a ~90-fold shift in substrate preference) plus a 26-fold improvement for the phytase at neutral pH. The authors self-assess the degree of automation as between level 3 (conditional automation) and level 4, with steps inside each module needing little if any human intervention. Released code covers the prediction models (MIT) and primer and worklist generation (BSD-3-Clause), archived on Zenodo (10.5281/zenodo.15233300, 10.5281/zenodo.15243671; both deposits declare MIT); the robotic workflows need the institutional facility and a commercial scheduler, and the authors list model and mutagenesis limitations. Distinct from PLMeAE, SAMPLE and the 2026 AI-native autonomous biofoundry.

name: Agentomics
domain: Autonomous machine-learning model development for biomedical data
inputs: A folder-based dataset split for a classification or regression task, with an optional data description and supplementary material; user-set run time, LLM backbone and validation metric
outputs: The best iteration's trained model with training and inference scripts and a conda environment, plus a PDF report of the approach and its train, validation and (if a test set is given) test metrics
notes: Agent from the Centre for Molecular Medicine and Biobanking, University of Malta, that runs iterative ML experiments inside a Docker container: an experiment-design model plans each iteration from earlier iteration summaries, and seven validated steps, from data exploration to prediction exploration, yield one working model per iteration. It can draw on pre-downloaded biomedical foundation models such as ESM-2, Nucleotide Transformer and ChemBERTa. In the Bioinformatics (ISMB 2026) evaluation on 20 protein-engineering, drug-discovery and regulatory-genomics datasets, it beat the other agent systems tested and produced new state-of-the-art models on 11 of 20 benchmarks. MIT licensed and pip-installable; runs with hosted LLM APIs or local Ollama models. Its outputs are predictive models, not biological hypotheses or experiments. Not the same as OpenMS/agentomics, a collection of pyopenms tools.

name: scBench
domain: Single-cell RNA-seq analysis by AI agents
inputs: AnnData snapshots captured immediately before an analysis step, with natural-language task prompts
outputs: Structured JSON answers scored pass/fail by deterministic graders on recovery of a key biological result, with per-model, per-task and per-platform accuracy, cost and agent trajectories
notes: LatchBio benchmark of single-cell RNA-seq analysis problems across six sequencing platforms and task categories from quality control to differential expression, run by agents in code-executing harnesses (the paper uses mini-SWE-agent capped at 100 steps). The arXiv v1 paper reports 394 problems in seven categories with 30 public examples; the current repository describes a revised set of 195 problems in six categories, of which six are public and the rest withheld to limit training contamination. The scbench repository (CLI, evaluation specs, results, trajectories) is Apache-2.0, but the graders and agent harness it depends on come from LatchBio's latch-eval-tools, whose licence file reserves all rights, and evaluation data are fetched from Latch Data through the Latch SDK. Earlier companion to the catalogued scBench-Long, which cites it and shares authors. Unrelated to the SCBench benchmarks for KV-cache methods and sports commentary.

name: SpatialBench (spatial biology agents)
domain: Spatial transcriptomics analysis by AI agents
inputs: Spatial-omics analysis states snapshotted immediately before a target step, with task prompts
outputs: Structured answers scored pass/fail by deterministic graders (numeric tolerance, multiple choice, marker-gene precision/recall, label-set Jaccard, distribution comparison) against a key biological result
notes: LatchBio benchmark covering five spatial transcriptomics platforms and seven task categories; the arXiv version reports 146 problems and the revised repository 159. Only 16 example evaluations, aggregate results and agent trajectories are public under Apache-2.0, and the full set is withheld to limit contamination. Task data load from latch:// nodes on the Latch platform. The graders and runner come from the required latch-eval-tools package, whose licence reads 'All rights reserved' and whose repository is archived. The paper reports large harness effects, with the authors' own Latch harness scoring highest for Opus-4.5 (61.7% vs 48.1% under Claude Code). Unrelated to other arXiv benchmarks named SpatialBench (spatial foundation models; multimodal spatial cognition) and SpatialBench-UC (text-to-image).

name: MetaClaw (metagenomics, HUST/BGI)
domain: Metagenomic and microbiome multi-omics analysis with provenance
inputs: A natural-language analysis request with a FlowHub path to raw shotgun reads, or pre-computed abundance and metabolite tables, plus sample metadata
outputs: Statistical results, figures and an HTML report, plus a per-job reproducibility bundle of parameters, generated scripts, container definitions, cloud submission specs and logs
notes: Metagenomics and microbiome multi-omics agent from Huazhong University of Science and Technology and BGI Genomics, built on the OpenClaw gateway. Quality control, host-read removal, profiling and assembly run as versioned flows on the FlowHub cloud platform; statistics, machine learning, figures and reports run in network-isolated containers from reference scripts the language model adapts to each cohort. The user confirms input bindings before any cloud job is submitted. On the full cohorts of four published studies (769 metagenomic profiles) it recovered 4/4, 3/3, 4/5 and 5/5 of the reported marker sets; downstream validity varied with the model backend and prompt detail. MIT licensed; end-to-end runs need a FlowHub account, and the July 2026 repository lacks the guides its README links to and benchmark files for one of the four studies. Independent of aiming-lab's MetaClaw (arXiv 2603.17187), a general self-improving OpenClaw agent.

name: PerturbTrace
domain: Feedback use by closed-loop perturbation-discovery agents
inputs: 17 screen-derived perturbation tasks (target, candidate identifiers, round budget) with hidden-oracle feedback under true, random or no-feedback conditions, run through a Codex-based launcher or a harness CLI with an externally supplied solver skill
outputs: Final hit recall and machine-readable run traces, plus stage-wise Feedback-to-State, State-to-Action and Action-to-Outcome diagnostics for each round-to-round transition
notes: Benchmark from DeepAutonomy Technology (Beijing) with 17 tasks derived from public perturbation resources: CRISPR knockout and activation screens (primary T cells, CAR-T, NK cells, phagocytosis, tau, choline recycling), DepMap/Achilles and Project DRIVE RNAi dependencies, GDSC2 drug response and JUMP Cell Painting morphology; some tasks are imported from the BioDiscoveryAgent task suite. It tests whether feedback appears in an agent's stated rationale, whether that rationale guides the next perturbation batch and whether the batch beats random sampling. The preprint runs BioDiscoveryAgent, Biomni, Codex and Codex with a restricted strategy on a GPT-5.5 backend against random, active-learning and LLM-guided Bayesian-optimisation baselines; 43 of 576 feedback-bearing transitions completed the full sequence, 25 of them under random feedback. The MIT repository ships task manifests, normalised oracle scores and hit sets, the harness and the trace evaluator, with a Codex-only runtime adapter; the non-agent baselines were not found in it, and the README describes a research release with fuller packaging planned. Distinct from PerTurboAgent.

name: PhenoAIR
domain: Mechanism-of-action inference from Cell Painting morphological profiles
inputs: Query compound Cell Painting profile and chemical structure (SMILES), plus a reference panel of profiled compounds with mechanism annotations
outputs: Predicted mechanism of action (or 'novel' in the open-set mode) with alternative candidates, a confidence level, written reasoning, and the full agent/controller trajectory, candidate memory and tool log
notes: Multi-agent framework that treats retrieved morphological neighbours as uncertain evidence to be weighed and sometimes rejected. A phenotype agent and a structure-side mechanism agent update a shared candidate memory; a rule-based controller picks further evidence views until it stops; an LLM arbiter then decides, followed by deterministic eligibility checks. Offline reference-set calibration scores source reliability, phenotype stability and mechanism confusion. Evaluated on a JUMP Cell Painting benchmark in controlled, realistic and open-world settings. MIT code; the Hugging Face dataset declares no licence. The repository states the default runtime does not yet reproduce the paper pipeline (uncalibrated retrieval, external mechanism-data adapters not yet included).

name: Enrich.AI
domain: Gene-set enrichment analysis and biological interpretation
inputs: A gene list with a short description of the biological context, in a conversational interface
outputs: Enrichment statistics, literature-grounded written interpretation and interactive visualisations
notes: Agent from the Ionian University (Corfu) that runs a reason-act-observe loop over five tools: enrichment against Enrichr gene-set libraries, Enrichr library queries, MyGene.info gene annotation, Europe PMC literature search, and text-mined paper annotations. It then writes an interpretation with six visualisation types. Uses Gemini 2.5 Flash by default; the code also accepts OpenAI-compatible APIs. The preprint's reliability evaluation on 50 MSigDB Hallmark gene sets used an LLM judge. MIT licensed, with tagged releases and a hosted Streamlit app; the chat interface is explicitly human-in-the-loop.

name: LungChat
domain: Conversational multi-omics analysis and drug repurposing in lung biology
inputs: Natural-language questions over curated single-cell and spatial lung datasets and connected literature, trial and perturbation resources
outputs: Tool-grounded analyses, figures, cell-type-resolved repurposing predictions and cited syntheses with parameter logs
notes: System from the LungMAP Data Coordination Center at Cincinnati Children's Hospital Medical Center. A supervisor agent splits a natural-language question into parallel, tool-grounded tasks across single-cell and spatial analysis, literature and clinical-trial retrieval and drug repurposing, and can run custom Python or R code in a sandbox; its DART module separates perturbations that reverse disease programs from those that reinforce them at cell-type level. From a single prompt it planned and ran a six-step idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis analysis that ranked saracatinib first, a compound already evaluated in the STOP-IPF trial, and a separate query recovered fluticasone propionate for COPD; both are computational prioritisations without new experimental validation. Evaluation used an author-built set of 100 test cases, including adversarial queries, scored by code checks and a GPT-4o judge. Use is user-initiated and conversational. The hosted service is free for research use but requires LungMAP sign-in and caps queries per user; the production codebase is not released and reproducibility materials are available on request.

name: PromptBio
domain: End-to-end computational biomedical research on a hosted platform
inputs: Natural-language research objectives with user-supplied or platform-retrieved public datasets, optionally with organization-provided scripts or pipelines
outputs: Reviewable analysis plans; executed analyses with retained code, parameters, environment details, outputs and logs; tables, figures and evidence-grounded written syntheses
notes: Commercial hosted platform from PromptBio Inc. Its agent harness, PromptGenie, turns a research objective into a reviewable multi-step plan, delegates to subagents and skills (omics pipelines, statistics, machine learning, literature and database retrieval, nf-core and organization-supplied pipelines, generated Python/R/shell code), runs steps in sandboxed environments and revises the plan after failures or new results. The preprint compares PromptGenie with Biomni and STELLA on PromptBio-Bench, the company's own 244-task benchmark, and with Biomni and Noah.bio on the 12-task Health subset of DeepResearch Bench II; it also reports vendor validation of selected omics and machine-learning skills and a HAQER regulatory-genomics case study in which a researcher confirmed the analysis plan before execution. All authors are company employees, and the underlying language models were not matched across the compared systems. No public code; access is through a sign-in portal with a free trial and paid tiers. ToolsGenie 2.0 (asa-toolsgenie-2-0) comes from the same company, and its preprint states that it is available on the PromptBio platform.

name: SynAgent (autonomous thin-film synthesis)

inputs: Campaign configuration (overview, target variable, allowed condition grid, fixed conditions), an OpenAI API key, and XRD patterns and SEM images delivered as MaiML files by an automated deposition and characterization platform
outputs: Proposed synthesis conditions with hypotheses and predictions, self-written analysis skills, synthesized films, and an explicit, revisable written understanding of the process
notes: Authors from the University of Tokyo, Rigaku and Mitsui Knowledge Industry replaced the Bayesian-optimization decision layer of the dLab automated thin-film platform with multimodal LLM agents (OpenAI Agents SDK, GPT-5.5). In one 18-experiment RF-sputtering campaign on LiCoO2 (001) films, the agents chose substrate temperatures, wrote their own XRD and SEM analysis skills and alternated proposals predicted to succeed and to fail. The paper states the films were synthesized and characterized without human intervention and describes no approval gate. Closure covered one controllable variable on a preset temperature grid with a fixed iteration budget. The paper offers code and data on request; the first author's MIT-licensed repository holds a cleaned port of the decision-layer code whose example settings differ from the published campaign, and the physical loop requires dLab. Unrelated to the humanoid-manipulation SynAgent (arXiv 2604.18557).

name: FermiLink
domain: Multidomain scientific simulation harness with an experimental-loop mode (autonomous quantum-transport measurements)
inputs: Markdown goal files, package knowledge bases for 150+ scientific codes or experimental skill repositories, an external coding agent (Codex, Claude Code, Gemini or OpenCode), laptop, HPC or lab-control workstation
outputs: Multi-day simulation and measurement campaigns, figure and paper reproductions, optimized scientific code, campaign memory and reports
notes: Harness from Tao E. Li's group (University of Delaware) that separates package knowledge bases from workflows and drives external coding agents. With Codex, its paper covers about 50 packages in nine domains and reproduces 74 of 132 published figures; a single-blinded test gave research-grade results on unpublished polariton problems when given detailed objectives and source code. A September 2026 preprint used its exploop mode to run cryogenic quantum-transport campaigns on MoS2 devices lasting up to six days without human intervention. Safety gate: all hardware access goes through a frozen acquisition script with hard-coded limits the agent cannot change; experts pre-build decision-tree Agent Skills for each device type, and the authors describe the autonomy as executing and adapting expert-defined workflows. The exploop code is in the AGPL-3.0 repository; the MoS2 transport skill repository named in its tutorial was not publicly reachable.

name: CAFES
aliases: Correlation-Aware Agentic Framework for Electronic Structure
domain: Agentic many-body electronic-structure simulation of strongly correlated systems
inputs: Natural-language or structured study/task requests; molecular geometries, POSCAR/CIF crystal structures or model-Hamiltonian lattices; local, Slurm or SSH-to-Slurm compute
outputs: Validated study and task specifications, generated PySCF input scripts, executed many-body calculations, correlation diagnostics, structured task/study reports with plots, and labelled datasets
notes: Rutgers University framework built on PySCF, with Block2, libDMET and fcDMFT for DMRG, DMET and DMFT, that organises calculations into studies and tasks. LLMs assist study planning and result interpretation; diagnostic-based method routing, validation, recovery and execution follow predefined rules, and the released package also runs without an LLM. Demonstrations: DMRG-CASSCF ground and low-lying excited states of lutein, adaptive DMET parameter scans of the extended honeycomb Hubbard model, and a CCSD-labelled dataset built from QM9 molecules. Active-space selection, refinements and other consequential steps require human approval. Apache-2.0 release with web, CLI, Python API and MCP interfaces.

name: CP-Agent
domain: Crystal-plasticity simulation workflows (PRISMS-Plasticity, CP-FEM and Taylor models)
inputs: One-sentence natural-language goal; typed CP tool set and optimizers; experimental or published reference stress-strain curves and target textures
outputs: Calibrated slip-hardening parameters, forward stress-strain/texture validations, recovered initial textures, chained five-pass rolling simulations, pole figures and visible reasoning traces
notes: ReAct-style GPT-4o agent from the University of Michigan (Aerospace Engineering). The harness is a minimal system prompt, typed tool schemas, a dispatcher and a safety-bounded iteration loop; numerical search is delegated to established optimizers. The same harness runs four case studies: SS316L calibration, OFHC copper forward validation and inverse texture recovery, and five-pass ZX31 magnesium rolling. Closure is computational only. The MIT-licensed code needs PRISMS-Plasticity, a commercial MATLAB licence with MTEX, and a paid LLM API. Different system from CrystalPlasticitySim and from unrelated arXiv systems also named CP-Agent (constraint programming, competitive programming, cell morphological profiling).

name: XRDreader
aliases: Experiment Reader Agentic Framework for X-Ray Diffraction
domain: Literature extraction of experimental powder-XRD figures and metadata
inputs: Search keywords, open-access publications (arXiv, Elsevier, Springer, CrossRef) and an LLM provider API key
outputs: Validated per-paper JSON records linking identified XRD figures to figure-level, text-derived and methodological metadata (no numerical digitisation of the patterns)
notes: Multi-agent pipeline by authors from the University of Rochester, NIST and other institutions that downloads and screens papers, identifies XRD figures, extracts and links metadata, and checks outputs against source evidence with an independent validation agent plus deterministic checks. On a curated 273-publication benchmark the paper reports up to 98.7% accuracy for XRD figure identification and 98.5% precision and 90.7% recall for the validated records. It does not yet digitise numerical diffraction data from figures. BSD-3-Clause code; benchmark data CC BY 4.0 on Zenodo. The README says the project was renamed from ERAF4XRD and will move to the DiffAI organisation. It builds databases rather than running experiments or simulations.

name: Rachel
inputs: Target molecule (SMILES), optional user priorities or constraints, and a host tool-capable general-purpose LLM agent
outputs: Multistep retrosynthetic route trees with sandbox-checked (RDKit) transformations, terminal precursor lists, planning and revision records, and route/reaction reports
notes: Stateful retrosynthesis-planning environment from the Hangzhou Institute of Medicine (Chinese Academy of Sciences), Beijing University of Chemical Technology and collaborators. A general-purpose LLM proposes and revises disconnections and chooses terminal precursors; Rachel executes candidate transformations in an RDKit-based sandbox and returns validation feedback, which the authors call a demonstration-level check that does not establish experimental feasibility. With GPT-5.5 the paper reports strict closure (complete route plus a separate post-hoc source audit of every terminal) for 111 of 120 PaRoutes targets and 24 of 25 RF25 targets. Planning is computational only: no laboratory synthesis was performed, route quality was scored by LLM evaluators, and RF25 routes had no human-expert review. Code and route atlas are CC BY-NC 4.0 (non-commercial); the README also links a login-gated web service.

name: MADE
inputs: Discovery agents or algorithms composed of generators, planners, scorers and filters (or an LLM orchestrator with tools); convex-hull task definitions for a chemical system; an oracle and an evaluation budget
outputs: Discovery efficacy and efficiency metrics for simulated campaigns (AF, EF, AUDC, mSUN) and discovered stable structures
notes: Benchmark environments from Diffractive Labs, the University of Oxford and Imperial College London (ICML 2026 poster per the arXiv comment). MADE simulates budgeted closed-loop campaigns in which an agent or algorithm proposes, evaluates and refines candidate materials, with discovery framed as finding thermodynamically stable compounds relative to a convex hull. Policies range from fixed pipelines of generators, planners and filters to a ReAct-style LLM orchestrator with tools, compared with baseline algorithms. The oracle is an ML interatomic potential (ORB, MACE) or an analytic function; DFT or experimental oracles are named as future work, so campaigns are computational only. MIT-licensed official repository; setup uses a Materials Project API key.

name: AutoMat (computational-materials reproduction benchmark)
aliases: Can Coding Agents Reproduce Findings in Computational Materials Science?
domain: Reproducing claims from computational materials-science papers
inputs: Expert-curated claim from a computational materials-science paper, with paper text (paywalled PDFs supplied by the user), metadata and, where available, author-provided code or data; the coding agent under test
outputs: Agent execution trace, generated artifacts and analysis report on whether the evidence supports the claim; LLM-judge reproducibility score (1-5, success = score of 4 or more) calibrated against SME judgments
notes: Johns Hopkins benchmark (COLM 2026) of 85 claims curated by subject-matter experts, in three regimes: from paper text, from released artifacts, and interpretation of provided outputs. Five agent settings were evaluated: a task-specific orchestrated agent, Claude Code (Opus 4.6, Sonnet 4.6, Kimi K2.5) and Codex CLI (GPT-5.4); the best reached a 53% success rate. Execution is computational only. Harness code is MIT. Claims are distributed separately as a gated Hugging Face dataset tagged CC BY 4.0, whose access form requires manual approval and agreement to non-commercial research use; 74 claims from 7 papers are released, others withheld pending publication, and paywalled papers are not included. Different system from the existing 'AutoMat' record (asa-automat-stem2mat-bench), a STEM microscopy-to-structure pipeline.
